Fundus of the right eye shows blurred disc margins (papilloedema) with ONH haemangioblastoma and epiretinal membrane with pseudohole (figures3 4).

report.source_text: MRI of the head showed multiple cystic space-occupying lesions in the posterior fossa (figure 9) and a well-circumscribed mass on the right optic nerve in the optic canal (figure 10). Since we suspected it to be a VHL disease, the most probable diagnosis was thought to be an optic nerve haemangioblastoma. MRI also showed bilateral enlarged kidneys with variable sized cortical cysts and a soft tissue space-occupying lesion in the mid part of left kidney (figure 11). A soft tissue lesion in the retroperitoneum, located in the right paramedian aspect of the L5 vertebra, is suggestive of an extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A woman in her late 30s presented with progressive bilateral vision loss (right > left) over 6 months, with prior brain surgery for cyst resection 7 years earlier and family history of similar complaints in a deceased brother. Ophthalmologic examination revealed bilateral optic nerve head hemangioblastomas with papilloedema and peripheral retinal hemangioblastoma (E001). MRI confirmed extensive multisystem involvement characteristic of VHL: multiple posterior fossa cystic lesions (CNS hemangioblastomas), right optic nerve mass, bilateral renal cysts with left renal soft tissue mass suspicious for renal cell carcinoma, and retroperitoneal mass suggestive of extra-adrenal pheochromocytoma (E006). The patient initially declined treatment and returned months later with severe vision deterioration to perception of light in the right eye and finger count in the left eye (E007). The diagnosis of VHL disease was established on clinical criteria based on multiple CNS hemangioblastomas, retinal hemangioblastomas, renal mass, suspected pheochromocytoma, and positive family history.
